draft_hypotheses: \mathcal F is a family of ideals of R containing R.
(I:a),(I,a)\in\mathcal F implies I\in\mathcal F for every ideal I and a\in R.
standalone_statement_tex: Let \(R\) be a ring and \(\mathcal F\) a family of ideals of \(R\) such that \(R\in\mathcal F\) and, for every ideal \(I\subseteq R\) and every \(a\in R\), the conditions \((I:a)\in\mathcal F\) and \((I,a)\in\mathcal F\) imply \(I\in\mathcal F\). Then every ideal maximal among the ideals not belonging to \(\mathcal F\) is prime.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-simple}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of $R$.
An ideal $I \subset R$ which is maximal with respect to the property
that $I \cap S = \emptyset$ is prime.
standalone_statement_tex:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of $R$.
An ideal $I \subset R$ which is maximal with respect to the property
that $I \cap S = \emptyset$ is prime.

draft_conclusions:
An ideal $I \subset R$ maximal with respect to not being
finitely generated is prime.

If every prime ideal of $R$ is
finitely generated, then
every ideal of $R$ is finitely generated\footnote{Later we will say
that $R$ is Noetherian.}.
source_enumerated_clauses:
An ideal $I \subset R$ maximal with respect to not being
finitely generated is prime.

If every prime ideal of $R$ is
finitely generated, then
every ideal of $R$ is finitely generated\footnote{Later we will say
that $R$ is Noetherian.}.
standalone_statement_tex: Let \(R\) be a commutative unital ring. (1) If \(I\subseteq R\) is maximal among ideals of \(R\) that are not finitely generated, then \(I\) is prime. (2) If every prime ideal of \(R\) is finitely generated, then every ideal of \(R\) is finitely generated.

draft_conclusions:
An ideal $I \subset R$ maximal with respect to not being
principal is prime.

If every prime ideal of $R$ is principal, then
every ideal of $R$ is principal.
source_enumerated_clauses:
An ideal $I \subset R$ maximal with respect to not being
principal is prime.

If every prime ideal of $R$ is principal, then
every ideal of $R$ is principal.
standalone_statement_tex:
Let $R$ be a ring.
\begin{enumerate}
\item An ideal $I \subset R$ maximal with respect to not being
principal is prime.
\item If every prime ideal of $R$ is principal, then
every ideal of $R$ is principal.
\end{enumerate}

draft_conclusions:
An ideal maximal among the ideals which do not contain a
nonzerodivisor is prime.

If $R$ is nonzero and every nonzero prime ideal in $R$
contains a nonzerodivisor, then $R$ is a domain.
source_enumerated_clauses:
An ideal maximal among the ideals which do not contain a
nonzerodivisor is prime.

If $R$ is nonzero and every nonzero prime ideal in $R$
contains a nonzerodivisor, then $R$ is a domain.
standalone_statement_tex:
Let $R$ be a ring.
\begin{enumerate}
\item An ideal maximal among the ideals which do not contain a
nonzerodivisor is prime.
\item If $R$ is nonzero and every nonzero prime ideal in $R$
contains a nonzerodivisor, then $R$ is a domain.
\end{enumerate}
